claim_text: The audio interface arrived with the monitor knob snapped off and the top panel cracked all around it.

_dev.why: radiating cracks across an aluminium faceplate are not how metal fails (it dents/scuffs); also doctored from ssl2_intact.jpg; serial-returner account

claim_text: Shirt arrived with a large tear on the front, it was already like this in the package.

_dev.why: tear looks plausible so Signal 1 is borderline, but the image is the intact listing photo (shirt_intact.jpg) with damage added — the reference comparison is the decisive catch

claim_text: There is a rip in the inner lining of the backpack near the pocket.

_dev.why: same image as C004 from a different account — perceptual-hash hard flag; also doctored from backpack_intact.jpg

claim_text: Backpack lining was torn on arrival, requesting a refund.

_dev.why: identical image to C003 from a different account — the reuse hard-flag fires

claim_text: The photo frame arrived with the glass completely shattered, shards everywhere inside the frame.

_dev.why: real shattered glass looks alarming, but glass genuinely shatters this way from impact; clean account; genuine photo with no doctored reference. The star false-positive case — proves the system passes real damage even when it looks dramatic.

claim_text: The storage tray was cracked and broken into pieces when the parcel arrived.

_dev.why: genuine breakage photo. The product HAS an intact listing reference (calcifer_intact.jpg), but this real damage shot is a separate photo so it does NOT match — demonstrating that genuine photos don't trip the reference signal, unlike the doctored fakes
